incipit: God, Which heareth all, even He sent His Angel, and took me from keeping my father's sheep, and
responsum: Anointed me with the oil of His mercy.
versus: The Lord That delivered me out of the mouth of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear

incipit: The Lord That delivered me out of the mouth of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear
responsum: He will deliver me out of the hand of mine enemies.
versus: God hath sent forth His mercy and His truth, and delivered my soul from among the lion's whelps.

incipit: Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands.
responsum: Because the hand of the Lord was with him, he smote the Philistine, and took away the reproach from Israel.
versus: Is not this David? Did they not sing one to another of him in dances, saying: Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands?

incipit: Ye mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew, neither let there be rain upon you
responsum: For there are the mighty of Israel fallen.
versus: All ye mountains that stand round about, the Lord look upon you but let Him pass by Gilboa

incipit: Thus saith the Lord: I took thee out of thy father's house, and appointed thee to be ruler over My people, over Israel.
responsum: And I was with thee whithersoever thou wentest, to establish thy kingdom for ever.
versus: And I have made thee a great name, like unto the name of the great men that are in the earth and have caused thee to rest from all thine enemies.

incipit: O Lord, Thou hast hearkened unto the prayer of thy servant, that I might build a temple unto thy Name,
responsum: O God of Israel, bless Thou, and hallow this house for ever.
versus: O Lord, Who keepest covenant with thy servants that walk before thee in all their heart.

incipit: Hearken, O Lord, unto the cry and to the prayer which thy servant prayeth before thee today, that thine eyes may be open and thine ears attend;
responsum: Toward this house day and night.
versus: Look down from thine high and holy place, O Lord, even from heaven thy dwelling.

incipit: Lord, when thy people shall turn again to thee, and shall pray unto thee in this house;
responsum: Then hear Thou in heaven, O Lord, and deliver them out of the hand of their enemies.
versus: If thy people sin against thee, and turn again, and repent, and come and pray unto thee in this house.

incipit: And it came to pass when the Lord would take up Elijah into heaven by a whirlwind
responsum: Elisha cried, and said: My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof.
versus: And as they still went on, and talked, behold, there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and parted them both asunder, and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
